# Policy-KB bijection audit — medicare_supplement_policy_desk / task 1

Revision 1. Auditor: independent KB-doc auditor. Scanned against
`tasks/medicare_supplement_policy_desk/medigap.extended.yaml` and the published corpus `docs/medigap/*.json`
(57 documents), with the five task-tool schemas as exposed at runtime. The blind audit was frozen and hashed
before any source-layer artefact was opened
(`audits/runtime_context/medicare_supplement_policy_desk/_freeze_r1.txt`).

**Entry conditions (Step 0).** Policy-side verdict PASSED at round 2 — cited from the brief. `check_docs.py` on
`medigap` and `check_traceability.py` on this difficulty both green; output lines supplied with the brief, not
re-run by the auditor. Runtime-visible view and a tool-shaped DB access path supplied; the DB side of the blind
audit was genuinely blind. Nothing missing from the input.

The structural correspondence, the base-policy scan, the retired surface and the `kb_to_source` findings are
common to the product and are recorded in full in `0.md` of this directory; they are not repeated here except
where this task's problems touch them. What follows is this task's own chain.

### Tool contracts

All seven parameters of `book_precoverage_restatement_aba9484f`, all seven of `repay_direct_benefit_f162ba18`
and all three of `settle_crossover_benefit_9f3dc765` are carried in their hubs with the same meaning, the same
form class and the same constraints as the runtime schema, including the thirteen-character Medicare claim
control number, the YYYY-MM-DD date form, the "never negative" and "2 decimal places" constraints, and the note
that the reversal and the repayment are *"booked against the policy as a negative payment"*. Owners match: the
restatement and the settlement are described as agent-side; the repayment as *"the policyholder's own tool: the
representative unlocks it and hands it over, and it is run by the customer themselves"*.

## kb_to_source

Every normative claim traced back; results as recorded in `0.md`. On this task's chain specifically:

- **No added business step.** Nothing asks the representative to confirm the restated figure with the
  policyholder, to review the claim before settling, or to notify anyone afterwards.
- **No cross-problem operational guidance.** Neither `crossover_benefit_settlement_desk_basis_f4af78d1` nor

- **No task world state written in as a policy fact.** `precoverage_line_restatement_computation_bab53e7e`
  illustrates on three paid lines each recording 40.00 on a policy that took effect before all of them;
  Aurelio's record is six paid lines recording 190/806/512/640/385/527 on a policy that took effect in the middle
  of them. `crossover_benefit_settlement_computation_cae09cc7` illustrates on Plan G with 240.00 approved and
  180.00 owing; the waiting line here is on High Deductible Plan G with 9400.00 approved and 10120.00 owing.
  `direct_benefit_repayment_computation_0cd18862` illustrates on payments of 96.00 and 84.00; the figures here
  are 40.00, 134.00 and 1180.00. No document states that this member has lines outside cover, an existing
  restatement or a waiting foreign travel claim.
- **The one class of sourced-but-misplaced sentence** (topic sentences from `rule` appearing in the baseline
  documents) is recorded once, under `dependency_form`.

## bijection_verdict

**KB-BIJECTION PASS.**

Every normative atom bearing on this task's chain — the three extended policies' baselines, all 15 of their
declared factors with every tier of every ladder, both `prerequisite` edges, the `medigap_benefit_payment`
overwrite and the base clauses it leaves in force, and the three tool contracts — is entailed by the published
documents at the same strength, with nothing dropped, nothing softened and nothing added. Revision 1; no earlier
revision exists.

### Policy-side notes (reported, not counted against this verdict)

**PS-4 — `retention_spread`'s ladder text is broader than its compute.** The source's tier conditions speak of
*"more than one line falls outside cover and each was a visit of its own"* and *"lines fall outside cover and
belong to one Medicare claim"*, and the document carries exactly that. The compute counts only the
**automatically crossed-over** lines outside cover (`auto_outside_cover_lines`, `distinct_claims_outside_cover`,
both filtered on `crossover_source='medicare_automatic_crossover'`). On this world the two readings select
different tiers — the source's compute takes tier 1 over lines A and B, while the documents' wording takes tier 2
over lines A, B and C, because B and C share the Medicare claim number `K26012045871` — and both multiply the
40.00 by two, so the scored 766.00 is unaffected. The divergence is between the source's prose and the source's
compute; the document renders the prose faithfully. Worth recording because a differently seeded world could
separate the two tiers numerically.

**PS-5 — `settled_line_selection` and `settlement_base` read different objects in prose and in compute.** The
prose selects a line and then works from *"its figures"*; the compute proxies the selection with
`largest_pending_owing` and takes the base from `largest_pending_approved` / `largest_pending_medicare_paid`,
which are maxima across all waiting lines rather than fields of the selected line. On this world they coincide
(the determined line `dd3d7daf…` carries both the largest owing, 10120.00, and the largest approved, 9400.00).
Again a source-side prose-versus-compute matter, faithfully rendered.

**PS-6 — the singular in edge B's prerequisite sentence.** The sentence reads *"the entry taking back what the
supplement paid on the lines that fall outside cover…"* — one entry, several lines. On this world one such entry
already stands (the adjustment of 2026-07-15 against line `66251bd0…`) while a second is still owed on line
`9a9d4d49…`, so an existential reading of "the entry" would treat the gate as already satisfied and produce
802.00 instead of 668.00. The distributive reading is the right one and the source confirms it — the
`condition` field reads *"a restatement entry taking back what the supplement paid on **the lines** outside cover
that reached someone other than the policyholder"* — and the documents entail it, because
`which_outside_cover_lines_are_restated_266fce42` makes *"the liability of those automatically crossed-over
lines"* (plural, both of them) what is restated and `amounts_recovered_from_others_c5c191d3` sets against the
figure *"the amounts those entries take back"* (plural). A solver must combine those two to read the gate
correctly; the sentence alone does not close it. Recorded as a policy-side note on the sentence's number, not as
a document defect.

## dependency_form

### KB-EXPLICIT RED — the computation documents announce that a variation exists

The same finding as recorded in `0.md`, and it bears on this task's chain at three of its five points. The full
statement of symptom, root cause and evidence is in `0.md`; the instances touching this task are:

1. `crossover_benefit_settlement_computation_cae09cc7`, section *"4. The yearly deductible"*:
   > *"A yearly deductible is taken from that amount before the share is worked out. No yearly deductible is
   > taken, the benefit carrying none."*
   The first sentence is in the source's `rule` and **not** in its `baseline.rule`. It announces the factor
   `travel_deductible_taken` — the 250.00 this task's scored figure turns on.

2. `precoverage_line_restatement_computation_bab53e7e`, section *"Which of them are restated"*:
   > *"Only some of those lines are restated here. Every line that falls outside cover is restated."*
   In `rule`, not in `baseline.rule`. "Only some" beside "every" can be reconciled only by a rule the reader is
   told lives elsewhere — the factor `lines_restated_here`, which is what confines this task's restatement to the
   automatically crossed-over lines.

3. `precoverage_line_restatement_computation_bab53e7e`, section *"What stays with the policyholder"*:
   > *"Part of that liability is not restated, because the coverage that was in force on those days leaves the
   > policyholder something of its own. The policyholder is left nothing, and the whole of the liability is
   > restated."*
   In `rule`, not in `baseline.rule`. It states not only that a variation exists but the reason it exists —
   which is the trigger condition of the factor `other_coverage_retention`, the factor that brings the
   Advantage specialist copay into this task at all.

(The other two instances, in `premium_account_settlement_computation_2871445e` §2 and
`overlap_premium_return_computation_7d397a4b` §4, bear on task 0 and are recorded in `0.md`.
`direct_benefit_repayment_computation_0cd18862` is clean on this point.)

### Everything else in the dependency-form scan: clean

- **Neither state-form sentence is restated as an action.** Both hubs restate their sentence only in the state
  form and only in the same document (*"Until such an entry stands on the claim record…"*). Neither names the
  performer, the resolving action, another policy, another document or a tool.
- **No other problem's tool name anywhere.** Mechanically checked across all 57 documents: each of the five
  medigap task tool names occurs in exactly one document, its own policy's hub, inside that hub's own invocation
  block; and none of the 27 task tool names belonging to the other five products occurs at all. In particular
  `crossover_benefit_settlement_desk_basis_f4af78d1` does not name `repay_direct_benefit_f162ba18`, and
  `direct_benefit_repayment_desk_basis_8b0134bf` does not name `book_precoverage_restatement_aba9484f`.
- **No dependency stated in a second document**, and **no chain aggregated**: no document sets the three
  problems of this task in an order, a table, a checklist, a roadmap or a step list. No example or FAQ walks
  across problems.
- **No wrong-versus-right contrast and no named mistake.**
- **No factor document tells the reader which tier applies.** None says "most policyholders", "typically", "in
  practice", or writes this member's rows in as a fact. Checked mechanically; the only matches for
  situation-naming language are the base eligibility conditions' phrase *"this member"*, carried verbatim from
  the source's own `condition` text in `advantage_exclusivity_basis_a4bc3e8e` and `single_supplement_holding_0d53025e`.
- **No factor document names or points at a computation document or another factor**, and no pointer wording
  ("as set out in", "see the", "refer to", "described elsewhere", "unless otherwise", "except as") occurs in the
  product at all.
- **Titles name general subjects.** *"Payment of a Crossover Claim Line Waiting on a Medicare Supplement
  Policy"*, *"Recovering Benefit the Supplement Paid the Policyholder Directly for Days It Did Not Cover"* and
  *"Putting Right a Crossover Line the Supplement Settled for a Day It Did Not Cover"* name the general subject
  each policy is defined by. None mirrors a caller's situation.
- **Findability without borrowed phrasing.** Each depended-on hub is reachable through the words the records and
  the prerequisite sentence use — "sent back", "recovered from the policyholder", "taken back", "days the policy
  did not cover", "lines outside cover" — not only through the blocked document's wording.

**Verdict: KB-EXPLICIT RED**, on the three statements above (five product-wide).

# revision_2 — verification of the round-1 REDs

Revision 1 above is preserved unmodified. This section is **verification, not a blind audit**: the auditor had
seen this task's GT from revision 1. The scope check, the criterion test, the both-directions removal check and
the whole-corpus regression check are set out in full in `0.md` of this directory and are not repeated; what
follows is this task's own chain.

**Scope verified independently:** `medigap.extended.yaml` unchanged (`9b11c3e10388e3a6…`), corpus hash
reproduced (`ba95f929a24e09d1…`), and exactly four documents — all of role `baseline` — have an mtime later than
the revision-1 freeze. Every one of the 15 documents this task's chain depends on other than the three
computation documents (the three hubs, the 15 factor documents, the facets and the base-policy documents) is
byte-identical to the revision audited.

## The three round-1 REDs on this task's chain

| # | Round-1 RED | Now reads | Closed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `crossover_benefit_settlement_computation_cae09cc7` §4: *"A yearly deductible is taken from that amount before the share is worked out."* | **§4 in full:** *"No yearly deductible is taken, the benefit carrying none."* | **yes** |
| 2 | `precoverage_line_restatement_computation_bab53e7e`: *"Only some of those lines are restated here."* | ***"**Which of them are restated.** Every line that falls outside cover is restated."* | **yes** |
| 3 | same document: *"Part of that liability is not restated, because the coverage that was in force on those days leaves the policyholder something of its own."* | ***"**What stays with the policyholder.** The policyholder is left nothing, and the whole of the liability is restated."* | **yes** |

RED 3 was the gravest of the five, because it did not merely announce that a variation exists — it stated the
**reason** one exists, which is the trigger condition of `other_coverage_retention`, the factor that brings the
Ridgecrest Advantage specialist copay into this task at all. The document now says nothing about other coverage
in this section; a solver learns that the Medicare Advantage enrollment matters only from the member's own
records, which is the intended route.

The two further traces the renderer found on this chain are also gone and both were real: *"What is left with
the policyholder falls across the lines outside cover"* (which announced the spreading rule
`retention_spread` applies) and *"Money already taken back is never taken back twice"*. On the second I
confirmed the renderer's reading against the source: that sentence is in
`medigap_ext_uncovered_day_line_restatement.rule` and **not** in its `baseline.rule`, while the parallel
principle **is** a sentence of `medigap_ext_dual_coverage_premium_return.baseline.rule` — so it is kept in the
return document and removed here, exactly as the source divides it. Nothing the source carries was dropped.

## The kept sentences on this chain

Three of the seven retentions touch this task, and each stays on the naming side:

- `crossover_benefit_settlement_computation_cae09cc7` §5: *"What counts toward that deductible is measured from
  the claim record: the liability the paid lines of the twelve months to date record is what counts."* It names
  the source of the measure and states the standard method in the same breath. Critically, it says **nothing**
  about restatements or about money recovered from the policyholder — the two kinds of entry that
  `deductible_counting_basis` turns on, and the two this task's writes create. A solver still has to find that
  factor from the claim record.
- `precoverage_line_restatement_computation_bab53e7e`: *"The liability of the lines restated is measured from
  the record."* beside *"Nothing is taken as the liability of those lines."* Naming, not affirm-then-deny.
- The `direct_benefit_repayment_computation_0cd18862` retentions are in the untouched document that served as
  the criterion at revision 1.

Every `baseline.rule` sentence of the three extended policies this task runs through is still carried: the
passive-voice renderings are all present (*"Every line that falls outside cover is restated."*, *"The
policyholder is left nothing, and the whole of the liability is restated."*, *"What is left with the
policyholder is not applied at all, no line falling outside cover."*, *"The whole amount recorded as
approved is taken."*), and the restatement policy's opening principle still stands in its hub
(`precoverage_line_restatement_desk_basis_77e35001`: *"A policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies
settles nothing for a day it was not in force…"*). The assembly sentences' terms are all still defined earlier
in their own documents, and both worked examples are intact and correct (crossover 240.00, precoverage 0.00).
